tone_statements.citation: Coupe, Alexander R. 2020. Northern Sangtam phonetics, phonology and word list. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 43(1): 147-189. doi:10.1075/ltba.19014.cou. [open prepublication version, DR-NTU hdl 10356/146605; contains first-hand Yimkhiung (Langa dialect) comparative data and a statement on its tones]
tone_statements.quote: The same tone-marking conventions are used for the marking of tone in the data of other Aoic languages presented in this paper, most of which similarly have systems of three level tonemes according to previous work (e.g. see Coupe 2003 and Temsunungsang 2009 for Ao dialects), as well as my own auditory impressions. The only exception is the Langa dialect of Yimkhiung, which appears to have just two contrastive tones in preliminary investigations. [p. 11] ... Three-register toneme systems appear to be common to most Aoic languages and are reported for Mongsen Ao (Coupe 2003) and Chungli Ao (Temsunungsang 2009). Preliminary auditory impressions suggest that Lotha has low, mid and high terrace-like tonemes, but the Langa dialect of Yimkhiung diverges in only appearing to have two contrastive level tones. [p. 21, sec. 7 Suprasegmental phonology]
tone_statements.summary: Lexical tone, register type: two contrastive level tones (preliminary, Langa dialect), one tone per syllable, vs. three levels in sister Aoic languages; phrasal boundary intonation may override lexical tones.

sources.note: Per Bruhn 2014 p. 172 (III.2.3.5 Tones), quoting and summarising Weidert: 'As with Sangtam, only Weidert 1987 records the tones of Yimchungrü, indicating two levels (1 = Low, 2 = High). Yimchungrü appears to have a register tone system, with one tone per syllable.' Weidert notes '[t]onal realization is redundantly marked for stopped syllables (occurs in Lotha, Sangtam, Yimchunger)' (1987: xvii) and gives underlying tones of main syllables in brackets (1987: xviii); Bruhn shows Weidert's own data has both tones on checked syllables (1mo(1)kɯʔ 'smoke' #302 vs 2a(2)hɯʔ 'to steal' #305). Not open…
